description: ML forecasting module: synthetic training data generator, persistence baseline model, Random Forest regression forecaster, chronological train/test split, MAE/RMSE metrics per horizon, and the ForecastingService class used by the predictions router. Depends on FEAT-001 (database models and schemas must exist). Independent of FEAT-003.
steps: Create backend/app/services/forecasting.py with the following: (a) `generate_synthetic_training_data(n_hours=72) -> pd.DataFrame` — produces a DataFrame with columns [timestamp, temperature_c, humidity_pct] using sinusoidal diurnal patterns with realistic noise; clearly documents that data is synthetic and unvalidated. (b) `build_feature_matrix(df: pd.DataFrame, horizon_minutes: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, pd.Series]` — adds lag features (1,2,3,6,12 readings back), rolling mean and std over 6 and 12 windows, hour_of_day, and creates target columns shifted by horizon steps; returns X, y_temp, y_humidity. (c) `train_models(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict` — for each horizon in [10,15,30]: splits df chronologically (80/20, no shuffle), trains a persistence baseline (predict last known value) and a RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42), computes MAE and RMSE on test split for both models, stores results. Returns model_store dict keyed by horizon. (d) class `ForecastingService` — singleton, lazily trains on first use (on synthetic data if fewer than 50 real readings exist), exposes `predict(recent_readings: list[SensorReading], horizons: list[int]) -> list[ForecastRecord]` method, and `get_metrics() -> dict` returning per-horizon MAE/RMSE for both baseline and RF. Marks all predictions with is_validated=False when trained on synthetic data. (e) Module-level `forecasting_service` singleton instance.

Wire the ForecastingService into the predictions router (backend/app/routers/predictions.py): call forecasting_service.predict() with the last 60 readings retrieved from DB, return ForecastRecord list plus metrics plus data_is_synthetic=True flag in PredictionsResponse.
Wire ForecastingService into main.py startup: after DB init, call forecasting_service.train() in a background thread so it does not block server start.
Add the forecast records produced by predict() to the DB in the APScheduler job in main.py (write ForecastRecord rows after each sensor reading).
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/predictions returns HTTP 200 with a forecasts list containing entries for horizons 10, 15, and 30
Each forecast entry has predicted_temperature_c and predicted_humidity_pct as floats
Response includes model_metrics with MAE and RMSE for each horizon for both baseline and random_forest
Metrics are real computed numbers — not fabricated. They may be poor on synthetic data; that is acceptable and expected.
verification: cd backend && python -c "from app.services.forecasting import ForecastingService; fs = ForecastingService(); fs.train(); m = fs.get_metrics(); print(m)"
